claims.text: The 2026/27 guidance uses four assessment tiers: AI-integrated, AI-assisted, AI-minimal and AI-prohibited. Follow the tier and permitted purposes in your assessment brief.

evidence.quote:
You may use AI tools for checking spelling and grammar mistakes only, with no other impact on the structure or content of the assessment. This includes AI tools such as Microsoft Word's grammar and spelling checker, and  not  GenAI tools such as Microsoft Copilot or ChatGPT. This is because using AI tools outside of these uses prevents fair assessment of your ability to achieve module learning outcomes.  
				 While completing AI-minimal assessments, you may find that some search tools you are using have GenAI features, such as source summarisation tools. Do not copy, paste or paraphrase information from these AI-generated summaries.
evidence.title: GenAI use in assessments

evidence.quote:
The University's guidelines on the use of GenAI in assessments appreciate that assistive technology using AI may have been recommended as part of the Disabled Students Allowance / Apprenticeship Needs Assessment Process. The majority of these tools are allowed even in AI-prohibited assignments. If there is any uncertainty with this please check with your Faculty Hub via SID:  https://sid.exeter.ac.uk/ 

 If you would like to discuss this further please engage with  AccessAbility .

coursework:E-E-TIERS.text: The 2026/27 guidance uses four assessment tiers: AI-integrated, AI-assisted, AI-minimal and AI-prohibited. Follow the tier and permitted purposes in your assessment brief.
coursework:E-E-TIERS.scope: AI-minimal allows spelling and grammar checking without other structural or content changes; it excludes GenAI tools such as ChatGPT and Copilot. Approved assistive-technology exceptions need their own scope.

evidence.quote: The University of Exeter follows a four-tier approach to GenAI use in assessments:

coursework:local-exeter-minimal.text: The 2026/27 guidance uses four assessment tiers: AI-integrated, AI-assisted, AI-minimal and AI-prohibited. Follow the tier and permitted purposes in your assessment brief.
coursework:local-exeter-minimal.scope: AI-minimal allows spelling and grammar checking without other structural or content changes; it excludes GenAI tools such as ChatGPT and Copilot. Approved assistive-technology exceptions need their own scope.

evidence.quote:
You may use AI tools for checking spelling and grammar mistakes only, with no other impact on the structure or content of the assessment. This includes AI tools such as Microsoft Word's grammar and spelling checker, and  not  GenAI tools such as Microsoft Copilot or ChatGPT. This is because using AI tools outside of these uses prevents fair assessment of your ability to achieve module learning outcomes.  
				 While completing AI-minimal assessments, you may find that some search tools you are using have GenAI features, such as source summarisation tools. Do not copy, paste or paraphrase information from these AI-generated summaries.

evidence.quote:
The University's guidelines on the use of GenAI in assessments appreciate that assistive technology using AI may have been recommended as part of the Disabled Students Allowance / Apprenticeship Needs Assessment Process. The majority of these tools are allowed even in AI-prohibited assignments. If there is any uncertainty with this please check with your Faculty Hub via SID:  https://sid.exeter.ac.uk/ 

 If you would like to discuss this further please engage with  AccessAbility .

coursework.en: The 2026/27 guidance uses four assessment tiers: AI-integrated, AI-assisted, AI-minimal and AI-prohibited. Follow the tier and permitted purposes in your assessment brief.

coursework.meaningEn: AI-minimal allows spelling and grammar checking without other structural or content changes; it excludes GenAI tools such as ChatGPT and Copilot. Approved assistive-technology exceptions need their own scope.
coursework.meaningZh: AI-minimal 只允许不改变其他结构或内容的拼写语法检查，不包括 ChatGPT、Copilot 等生成式 AI；获准辅助技术的例外须另看适用范围。

exams.en: The four-tier framework does not establish blanket AI permission in an exam. Check the tier and instructions for the actual assessment.

exams.meaningEn: The reviewed source covers assessments; exam delivery, supervision and assistive adjustments require specific instructions.

disclosure.en: For AI-integrated and AI-assisted assessments, include GenAI prompts and, where possible, links to outputs in the submission. Record direct and indirect use; reference direct use.
disclosure.zh: 在 AI-integrated 及 AI-assisted 考核中，提交物须包含提示词，并尽可能附输出链接；记录直接与间接使用，并引用直接使用的内容。
disclosure.meaningEn: Submission records and references are different requirements. Translation beyond a word or short phrase needs agreement in the assessment brief.
disclosure.meaningZh: 提交记录与参考引用属于不同要求；将超过单词或短语的内容翻成英语，须由考核说明明确同意。
